crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Pathology Detection and Scan Triage
children.blurb: Pathology detection and scan triage covers automated flagging of suspicious findings in radiology images such as chest X-rays, CT scans, mammograms, and pathology slides, and the ordering of unread studies by urgency.

children.name: Synthetic Imaging from Existing Scans
children.blurb: Synthetic imaging from existing scans is the creation of new medical images that resemble real patient scans but are generated by computational models rather than acquired from a patient.

children.name: Anatomical Models and 3D Printing
children.blurb: Anatomical models and 3D printing in diagnostic imaging and radiology involve converting patient-specific imaging data, typically CT or MRI, into physical replicas of organs, bones, vessels, or pathology.

children.name: Point of Care Ultrasound Enhancement
children.blurb: Point of care ultrasound enhancement covers AI systems that assist clinicians at the bedside with acquiring, interpreting, and acting on ultrasound images.

children.name: Radiomics
children.blurb: Radiomics is the high-throughput extraction of quantitative features from standard medical images, turning regions of interest into structured data for analysis.

sections.body: This field applies machine learning to medical images such as X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, and ultrasound. Right now AI systems are reading scans to flag possible fractures, bleeds, lung nodules, and strokes, and they are sorting worklists so urgent cases get a radiologist's attention sooner. Some tools generate a synthetic CT from an MRI or enhance a low quality ultrasound image in real time. Others turn scan data into printable 3D models of a patient's anatomy for surgical planning. Radiomics extracts hundreds of measurable features from images, like texture and shape, to look for patterns that are not visible to the eye.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The most mature work is in narrow detection tasks, where models can match or approach a radiologist on a specific finding in a clean dataset, but real world performance drops when equipment, patient populations, or imaging protocols change. Synthetic imaging and 3D model generation are usable in some hospitals, yet they still require human checks because errors can be subtle and clinically important. Point of care ultrasound enhancement is promising but often depends on the operator's skill and the device. Radiomics remains largely research facing, with reproducibility problems across scanners and institutions. Honest limits include a shortage of large, labeled, multi site datasets and the fact that most tools are assistive, not autonomous.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to understand how AI finds disease and prioritizes scans should start with Pathology Detection and Scan Triage, which covers the core use case. Synthetic Imaging from Existing Scans explains how one scan type can be turned into another, and it pairs naturally with Anatomical Models and 3D Printing, where that data becomes a physical or digital model for planning. Point of Care Ultrasound Enhancement shows a different branch, where AI cleans up live images at the bedside rather than reading them after the fact. Radiomics sits at the research edge, turning images into numbers for pattern discovery, and it connects back to detection because those features can feed the same triage models.
